extraction.Name: Levie Prue
extraction.Refused/Protested: No, it was my understanding that I had to take it and I was going to war at that time
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: I first mortgaged and then sold it
extraction.Buyer: not stated; mortgage for $2000; sold for $3000.00 more and the purchaser paid the tax
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: I did not want the patent in the first place but knew that I could not pay the taxes while I was gone to war and used the mortgage as a means of getting something out of it rather than let the taxes take it while I was gone
extraction.Occupation/Income: I work at odd jobs and farm
extraction.NOTES: Patent delivered by the Farmer at Okreek in 1918; wife and three children dependent on him; not in good health; does not remember making an application for the patent; was going to war at the time of patent; banker offered loan on the place; states he had heard soldiers were exempt from tax during the war but had not heard it at that time; cash deal confirmed; not sure if he signed a receipt for the patent but thinks he did
